statement: The chrome.debugger API attaches to tab targets to transport Chrome DevTools Protocol commands for DOM, network, and input control.
quote: The chrome.debugger API serves as an alternate transport for Chrome's remote debugging protocol. Use chrome.debugger to attach to one or more tabs to instrument network interaction, debug JavaScript, mutate the DOM and CSS, and more.

statement: Chrome DevTools Protocol Input.dispatchMouseEvent and Input.dispatchKeyEvent dispatch browser-level input events directly to the page.
quote:
"name": "dispatchMouseEvent",
"description": "Dispatches a mouse event to the page.",

statement: Since Chrome 125, browser.debugger supports flat child sessions via sessionId to command out-of-process iframes without separate attach calls.
quote:
Starting in Chrome 125, the browser.debugger API supports flat sessions. This
lets you add additional targets as children to your main debugger session and
message them without needing another call to browser.debugger.attach. Instead,
you can add a sessionId property when calling browser.debugger.sendCommand to
identify the child target you would like to send a command to.

statement: Extension content scripts execute by default in an isolated world hidden from host page scripts and other extensions.
quote:
Key term: An isolated world is a private execution environment that isn't accessible to the page or other
extensions. A practical consequence of this isolation is that JavaScript variables in an extension's
content scripts are not visible to the host page or other extensions' content scripts.

statement: MDN confirms that ISOLATED is the default content script execution environment sharing the DOM while isolating global scopes.
quote:
The default content scripts execution environment.
This environment is isolated from the page's context: while they share the same document, the global scopes and available APIs differ.

statement: The ExecutionWorld enum lets extensions target ISOLATED or MAIN world shared with host page JavaScript.
quote:
"ISOLATED"
Specifies the isolated world, which is the execution environment unique to this extension.
"MAIN"
Specifies the main world of the DOM, which is the execution environment shared with the host page's JavaScript.

statement: Mozilla documents MAIN world execution as sharing the web page environment without isolation.
quote:
The web page's execution environment.
This environment is shared with the web page without isolation.

statement: Chrome terminates an MV3 extension service worker after 30 seconds of inactivity or when a single request exceeds 5 minutes.
quote:
Normally, Chrome terminates a service worker when one of the following conditions is met:
After 30 seconds of inactivity. Receiving an event or calling an extension API resets this timer.
When a single request, such as an event or API call, takes longer than 5 minutes to process.

statement: Active browser.debugger sessions, WebSocket traffic, and runtime.connectNative ports keep or extend Chrome MV3 service worker lifetimes.
quote:
Active debugger sessions created using the browser.debugger API now keep the service worker alive. This prevents service workers from timing out during calls for this API.
Chrome 116
Chrome 116 introduced the following service worker lifetime improvements:
Active WebSocket connections now extend extension service worker lifetimes. Sending or receiving messages across a WebSocket in an extension service worker resets the service worker's idle timer.

statement: The storage.session area stores up to 10 MB in memory across worker restarts and restricts content script access by default.
quote: Session storage holds data in memory while an extension is loaded. The storage is cleared if the extension is disabled, reloaded, updated, and when the browser restarts. By default, it's not exposed to content scripts, but this behavior can be changed by calling browser.storage.session.setAccessLevel(). The storage limit is 10 MB (1 MB in Chrome 111 and earlier).

statement: Safari 16.4 supports storage.session for fast in-memory state preserved across non-persistent background page loads.
quote: The storage.session API, now supported in Safari 16.4, enables extensions to store data in memory for the duration of the browser session, making it a useful tool for storing data that takes a long time to compute or is needed quickly between non-persistent background page loads.

statement: Native messaging exchanges UTF-8 JSON payloads over stdin and stdout preceded by a 32-bit native byte-order length header.
quote:
Chrome starts each native messaging host in a separate process and communicates with it using
standard input (stdin) and standard output (stdout). The same format is used to send messages in
both directions; each message is serialized using JSON, UTF-8 encoded and is preceded with 32-bit
message length in native byte order.

statement: Mozilla corroborates that native messaging frames UTF-8 JSON with an unsigned 32-bit native byte-order length prefix on stdin and stdout.
quote:
On the application side, you use standard input to receive messages and standard output to send them.
Each message is serialized using JSON, UTF-8 encoded and is preceded with an unsigned 32-bit value containing the message length in native byte order.

statement: Firefox Manifest V3 does not support background.service_worker and executes non-persistent event pages via background.scripts.
quote:
Firefox:
background.service_worker is not supported (see Firefox bug 1573659).
supports background.scripts (or background.page) if service_worker is not specified or the service worker feature is disabled.

statement: Unlike Firefox MV3 event pages, Chrome Manifest V3 forbids background or event pages and mandates service workers.
quote: The getBackgroundPage() methods discussed in this section cannot be used in a cross-browser extension, because Manifest Version 3 extensions in Chrome cannot use background or event pages.

statement: Safari Web Extensions package standard web extension code inside native Xcode app containers for App Store distribution.
quote:
This release brings support for Safari Web Extensions. They are a type of extension primarily built with JavaScript, HTML, and CSS packaged with native apps. This allows extension developers to maintain a single codebase that can be packaged for other browsers.
It also means developers with extensions for other browsers can easily bring their projects to Safari with a command-line tool. It jump-starts your development by converting your web extension into an Xcode project, ready to build and test.

statement: MDN confirms that while Chrome, Firefox, and Edge distribute zipped manifests, Safari packages extensions like native apps.
quote: Firefox, Chrome, Edge, and Opera all use a simple zip format that requires the manifest.json file to be at the root of the zip package. Safari requires extensions to be packaged in a similar way to apps.

statement: Extensions can retrieve both open and closed ShadowRoot instances via dom.openOrClosedShadowRoot without main-world interception.
quote: Gets the open shadow root or the closed shadow root hosted by the specified element. If the element doesn't attach the shadow root, it will return null.

statement: Firefox supports browser.dom.openOrClosedShadowRoot and element.openOrClosedShadowRoot to return closed shadow roots to extensions.
quote: In Firefox, the equivalent property is element.openOrClosedShadowRoot. This read-only property represents the shadow root hosted by the element, regardless of whether its mode is open or closed.

statement: CDP DOM.describeNode traverses iframes and shadow roots when pierce is enabled without starting node tracking.
quote:
"name": "pierce",
"description": "Whether or not iframes and shadow roots should be traversed when returning the subtree\n(default is false).",

statement: Synthetic DOM clicks via HTMLElement.click() or EventTarget.dispatchEvent() set Event.isTrusted to false.
quote: The isTrusted read-only property of the Event interface is a boolean value that is true when the event was generated by the user agent (including via user actions and programmatic methods such as HTMLElement.focus()), and false when the event was dispatched via EventTarget.dispatchEvent(). The click event fired through HTMLElement.click() sets the isTrusted property to false.

statement: The W3C WebExtensions Community Group standardizes a shared platform core while explicitly expecting vendor-specific API capabilities.
quote:
Given this, we expect browser vendors to offer APIs and capabilities beyond what's specified.
Of course, the need for autonomy must be balanced against the need to provide
developers with a consistent and interoperable platform. To that end, we seek to
specify a common platform that includes the base extension model, permissions
model, and a common core of APIs for web extensions that all browsers can build
upon.

statement: W3C WebDriver BiDi specifies input.performActions to dispatch user-agent-level input sequences outside browser-specific extension APIs.
Native messaging enforces a 1 MB maximum single-message size from the host to Chrome and 64 MiB from Chrome to the host.
quote:
The maximum size of a single message from the native messaging
host is 1 MB, mainly to protect Chrome from misbehaving native applications. The maximum size of the
message sent to the native messaging host is 64 MiB.

statement: First-party browser-control custody persists tab ownership and epoch fencing in chrome.storage.session and rejects stale pageId or expired commands.
quote: First-party browser-control custodian persists tab ownership and epoch fencing in chrome.storage.session and rejects stale pageId or expired commands before dispatching debugger input.

statement: Chrome 136 ignores --remote-debugging-port and --remote-debugging-pipe on the default Chrome user data directory unless a custom --user-data-dir is supplied.
quote:
Therefore, from Chrome 136 we're making changes to the behavior of
--remote-debugging-port and --remote-debugging-pipe. These switches
will no longer be respected if attempting to debug the default Chrome data
directory. These switches must now be accompanied by the --user-data-dir
switch to point to a non-standard directory.

statement: Firefox does not implement Chrome's debugger API, causing CDP-dependent extension controls to fail without a host-assisted fallback.
quote:
Debugger API
In Firefox: Chrome's debugger API is not implemented.

statement: Scripts executing in the MAIN world lack extension APIs and expose their logic and data to page interception and interference.
quote:
Scripts in this environment don't have any access to the APIs that are only available to content scripts.
Warning: Due to the lack of isolation, the web page can detect and interfere with the executed code.
Do not use the MAIN world unless it is acceptable for web pages to read, access, or modify the logic or data that flows through the executed code.

statement: Because content scripts share the renderer process with web pages, a compromised renderer can leak data or hijack content-script privileges.
quote:
To interact with DOM of web pages, content scripts need to execute in the same renderer process as
the web page. This makes content scripts vulnerable to leaking data via side channel attacks
(e.g., Spectre), and to being taken over by an attacker if a malicious web page compromises
the renderer process.

statement: Enterprise runtime_blocked_hosts policies block browser.debugger.attach() and detach active debugger sessions if any frame navigates to a restricted host.
quote:
Calling browser.debugger.attach() fails with the error
"This page cannot be scripted due to an ExtensionsSettings policy." if the URL of the target, or of any frame in it, matches
runtime_blocked_hosts. If an attached target, or any frame in it, navigates to a blocked host, Chrome detaches the debugger.

statement: Chrome forcibly terminates an extension's debugger session via onDetach when the tab closes or when Chrome DevTools opens on the tab.
quote: Fired when browser terminates debugging session for the tab. This happens when either the tab is being closed or Chrome DevTools is being invoked for the attached tab.

statement: Service workers must validate sender.origin and sanitize payloads before forwarding content-script messages to a native messaging host.
quote:
Warning: Because content scripts share a renderer process with untrusted web
pages, your service worker must validate sender.origin (or sender.url) and
sanitize the message payload before forwarding any data to the native host.

statement: A 20-second WebSocket keepalive interval resets the idle timer before Chrome's 30-second service worker shutdown threshold.
quote: // Set the interval to 20 seconds to prevent the service worker from becoming inactive.

statement: Chrome MV3 offscreen documents run hidden DOM APIs immune to site CSP restrictions while exposing only the runtime messaging API.
quote:
Service workers don't have DOM access, and many websites have content security policies that
limit the functionality of content scripts. The Offscreen API allows the extension to use DOM
APIs in a hidden document without interrupting the user experience by opening new windows or
tabs. The runtime API is the only extensions API
supported by offscreen documents.

statement: The activeTab permission restricts tab host access until an explicit user gesture occurs and revokes access on cross-origin navigation or closure.
quote:
In contrast, an extension with the "activeTab" permission only obtains access to a tab in response
to an explicit user gesture. If the extension is compromised the attacker would need to wait for the
user to invoke the extension before obtaining access. And that access only lasts until the tab is
navigated or is closed.

statement: WXT compiles separate extension builds and manifests per target browser and manifest version from shared typed entrypoints.
quote: When building an extension with WXT, you can create multiple builds of your extension targeting different browsers and manifest versions.

statement: Scripts injected into the MAIN world are governed by the host web page's Content Security Policy rather than the extension CSP.
quote:
When a content script is injected into the main world, the CSP of the page
applies.

statement: First-party MAIN-world bridging captures native postMessage and hasOwnProperty bindings at load time and emits allowlisted descriptors only.
quote: First-party MAIN-world fiber bridge captures native window.postMessage and Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty bindings at load time and never forwards raw request arguments across the world boundary.
